questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
1. Good grading of the teaching systems.
2. The spoken language is english.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not come into the housing I applied for, nobody informed that there was something called midterms instead of exams and they graded my courses incorrectly in the end so I had to send a complain about it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The adress to collect the key was not clearly indicated and the introduction to different webpages was very poor.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: You had to search most assistance yourself but you had a contact person you could reach out to in case you had questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I did not end up in any of the ones I choose beforehand they put me in a house with people that I had nothing in common with and they were studying at other levels than me. I wish I had not stayed on campus but they did not inform me that I did not get into the kind of housing I applied for. My room was so noisy with road construction in the entire period and a lot of cars passing by not to mention the bed was awfull so I had to buy an airmadress to sleep.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I am happy we had a kitchen since the meal plans are expensive. You have to buy everything for the kitchen yourself and when I move it other people filled the fridge and freezer so I could not fit my things inside.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Choose to live in West if you want to have a change to hang out with other exchange students. If you end up in a house you might risk not being included in the social activities taking place. Otherwise search for off campus options and do not pick the meal plan at campus if you wanna save your money a bit.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The house I lived in felt very old, the pressure in the shower was not good and some of the windows could not open and close so sometimes it was very cold to sleep.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy to get a student card, but it was not very clear that you did not need a meal plan and where to collect my keys.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You just apply though KU and you get a contact person at University of Guelph that you can go to and they will help you solve different difficulties.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The contact person at University of Guelph.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Easy as the contact person just helped me to register for the ones I wanted. The only complicated thing was to find courses which would not overlap each other.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just use the contact person, your mail and courselink and you will be good.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: One of the courses was a class of 10 people and it was hard to do group work since it was not that many people in each class. One of the professors was not very clear about deadlines and how to find materials for the courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Master level courses require more effort to pass so be aware to pay more attention to your courses if you are a master student.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. A lot of assignment and midterms witch forms your final grade. One one of my courses had a final exam they rest was based on what I made in the period while the course took place.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
FARE3250
FARE3320
FOOD4190
FOOD4260

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go for the ones with a lot of group work so you do not have to struggle so much to make points in the courses. It is easier to form groups with Canadians since they know how the school system works and how the reports should look like.

questions.answer: Printing out notes for exams. The cost of trips with different clubs at the school.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food at the school was more expensive than I expected it to be.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have so many oppurtunities at the school to join sport, outdoor life and meet up with other students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Icehockey, board games, trivia nights

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Pay attention to free pizza nights that way you can really save a lot of time and money on food and you get to be social at the same time. Go to activities where you can win free prizes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Nigara falls, Toronto maple leaves

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just go for different events at the University.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Unhealthy food

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Easy communication and wildlife areas.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Remember to go to your midterms, eat free pizza and hand out at the pub inside the University.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just be open minded and join events. Pay attention to how much it requires to pass courses.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To meet so many wonderful people and try new courses.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To find materials for the different courses and to find the right information for the courses.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
